title: definition node
description:
What a thing is, with its typed attributes. Identity is the only question the kind asks: does the domain care *which one* it is, or only *what it holds*?

An entity has identity that persists through change. A value object is defined entirely by its attributes and is replaced rather than modified. Most things a first pass calls entities are value objects. An aggregate root is an entity that is also the aggregate's entry point; a read model exists to be queried and holds no invariant; a domain error names a refusal, and it is a definition rather than a rule because a rejection references the error it produces.

The set of definition nodes is the ubiquitous language. A synonym is declared in `aliases` and appears in no body.

attributes.description: What this definition holds, fully typed against the closed primitive vocabulary. Where the material does not state a length, a precision or a currency, the parameter is left absent rather than chosen.

identity.description: Which attributes form this definition's identity. `strategy` inherits the base's declared default and is stated only where this definition differs.

then.description: A definition the domain asks *which one* about declares what forms that identity. A value object and a domain error declare none.

x-alternation: Everything this kind requires, or a declared gap naming what is missing. A prohibition is not excused: a gap says a fact is absent and cannot make a forbidden field allowed.
